headline: Life cycles are the stages from birth to death to new life—patterns that repeat across generations
universal_truth: Everything has seasons; understanding cycles helps you navigate where you are and what comes next
fun_facts: Mayflies live as adults for only 24 hours—their entire purpose is reproduction
Some jellyfish can reverse their life cycle, effectively becoming immortal
Salmon are born in freshwater, live in salt water, and return to freshwater to spawn and die
discussion_questions: What life cycle stage are you in currently?
How does understanding cycles change how you approach current challenges?
What stage is coming next for you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Birth, growth, reproduction, death. Every living thing follows a cycle—not a line but a circle. What dies feeds what's born. Generations connect through these repeating patterns. Life isn't just living; it's cycling.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Life cycles seem obvious, but they contain wisdom. Each stage has its purpose and challenges. What does thinking in cycles teach us?
cliff.prompt: What's the value of cycle thinking?

options.text: Cycles reveal that each stage is temporary and purposeful—understanding where you are helps you do that stage's work and prepare for what's next
options.response: Yes. Youth is for growth. Maturity is for contribution. Each stage has its task. Fighting your stage wastes energy; embracing it lets you complete it and move on.
They describe, but they also prescribe—each stage has appropriate work...

q1.title: Stage-Appropriate Work
q1.script: Each life stage has appropriate work. Young animals learn and grow. Adults reproduce and provide. Elders teach. Doing the right work at the right stage is efficiency; fighting it is waste.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Stage-Appropriate Work"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Transition Points
q2.script: Between stages are transitions—often difficult. Adolescence between childhood and adulthood. Retirement between work and rest. Transition is inherently uncomfortable; it's moving between stable states.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Generational Connection
q3.script: Cycles connect generations. What one generation produces, the next consumes and builds upon. You're part of a cycle larger than your individual life—receiving from the past, contributing to the future.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Everything has seasons. Understanding cycles helps you navigate where you are and what comes next. Do the work of your current stage.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 262. Tomorrow, we'll explore how life makes more life—reproduction. Until then, identify what stage you're in and its appropriate work.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Stage Assessment - Where Are You in the Cycle?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify current life stage and appropriate work
growTrack.activity: What life stage are you in—in career, relationships, personal development? What's the appropriate work of this stage? What stage is coming next? Align your efforts with your stage for maximum effectiveness.
